words.tr: adj. 真实性可疑的；杜撰的
words.ex: The story about the ghost is apocryphal.
words.ex_cn: 关于鬼魂的故事是不可信的。
words.en: An apocryphal story is one that is probably not true or did not happen, although it is often told and believed by some people to be true.

words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.ex: The flowers exude a sweet smell.
words.ex_cn: 花朵散发出甜美的香味。
words.en: If someone exudes a quality or feeling, or if it exudes, they show that they have it to a great extent.

words.ex: He gesticulates when he talks about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 当他谈论旅行时，他会用手势示意。
words.en: If you gesticulate, you make movements with your arms and hands, usually while you are describing something that is difficult to express in words.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

words.ex: The small village lies on the periphery of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于城市的外围。
words.en: The outer limits or edge of an area or object.

words.tr: n. 善于讲故事的人；健谈者
words.ex: He was known as a raconteur, always able to captivate an audience with his stories.
words.ex_cn: 他以健谈著称，总能用他的故事吸引听众。
words.en: A raconteur is someone who is good at telling stories in an interesting and amusing way.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr: n. 军人的配备；（为特定活动提供的）服装，装备
words.ex: The soldier cleaned his accoutrements before the parade.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在阅兵前清理了他的军用装备。
words.en: The equipment or accessories needed for a particular activity or role.

words.tr:
adj. 愤愤不平的；委屈的；受害的
v. 令委屈；令苦恼；侵害；“aggrieve”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt aggrieved by the unfair treatment she received.
words.ex_cn: 她因受到不公平的对待而感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you feel aggrieved, you feel upset and angry because you think that you have been treated unfairly.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；暴躁的；脾气不好的
words.ex: He is a choleric man who shouts when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个易怒的人，一生气就大喊大叫。
words.en: A choleric person is someone who gets angry very easily.

words.tr: v. 表现；举止；一致；相称
words.ex: He comports himself with kindness.
words.ex_cn: 他以友善的方式表现自己。
words.en: If you comport yourself in a particular way, you behave in that way.

words.tr: v. 使慌张；使窘迫；使不安
words.ex: The sudden noise disconcerted her.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让她感到不安。
words.en: If something disconcerts you, it makes you feel anxious, confused, or embarrassed.

words.ex: The forest is home to a rich fauna.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是丰富动物群的家园。
words.en: The animals of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.

words.tr: v. 置于…之间；插入；插嘴；介入
words.ex: The mediator tried to interpose before the situation escalated.
words.ex_cn: 调解人试图在局势升级之前进行干预。
words.en: If you interpose something between two people or things, you place it between them. If you interpose, you interrupt with a comment or question.

words.tr:
v. 抢劫；掠夺
n. 袭击
words.ex: The soldiers marauded through the village, taking whatever they wanted.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里四处掠夺，拿走了他们想要的一切。
words.en: To maraud means to roam around in search of things to steal or people to attack.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: The palace had opulent carpets and golden chandeliers.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿里有华丽的地毯和金色的吊灯。
words.en: Having or displaying great wealth or richness.

words.tr:
n. （古罗马的）贵族；名门望族；有教养的人；罗马帝国的地方官
adj. 贵族的；贵族似的；上流社会的
words.ex: She was born into a patrician family.
words.ex_cn: 她出生在一个贵族家庭。
words.en: A patrician is a person of high birth or noble status, especially in ancient Rome.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: The muscle showed signs of atrophy after the injury.
words.ex_cn: 受伤后，肌肉出现了萎缩的迹象。
words.en: Atrophy refers to the wasting away or decrease in size of an organ or tissue, typically as a result of disease, injury, or lack of use.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.ex: He receives a small emolument for his part-time job.
words.ex_cn: 他因兼职工作获得少量报酬。
words.en: A payment made to someone for work or services, typically in the form of a salary or fee.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.tr: v. 反复灌输；谆谆劝导
words.ex: Parents try to inculcate good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To inculcate is to teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；无法估计的
words.ex: Her kindness is inestimable.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良是无法估量的。
words.en: If you describe the value, benefit, or importance of something as inestimable, you mean that it is extremely great and cannot be calculated.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.tr: n. 要求严格纪律的人；严格执行纪律者
words.ex: The sergeant was a martinet who insisted on absolute obedience from his troops.
words.ex_cn: 这位中士是一个严格执行纪律的人，他坚持要求他的部队绝对服从。
words.en: A martinet is someone who demands strict adherence to rules and discipline.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.ex: He follows a strict regimen to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循严格的作息计划来保持健康。
words.en: A regimen is a systematic plan or course of action intended to improve or maintain health, or a prescribed routine of diet, exercise, or manner of living.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.tr:
n. 斯多葛派人；坚忍克己之人；
adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的；
words.ex: He is a stoic who never shows his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不流露情感的斯多葛派人。
words.en: Someone who is stoic does not show their feelings or complain when bad things happen to them.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: He is zealous about helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他热心帮助别人。
words.en: If someone is zealous, they are enthusiastic and eager about something, especially something they believe in very strongly.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.ex: He kept his composure during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中保持了冷静。
words.en: The state of being calm and in control of your emotions.

words.ex: The old edifice stands near the river.
words.ex_cn: 那座古老的建筑坐落在河边。
words.en: An edifice is a large, impressive building.

words.ex: He ensconced himself in the armchair with a book.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己安顿在扶手椅里看书。
words.en: If you ensconce yourself somewhere, you settle yourself there in a safe, comfortable, or secret place.

words.tr:
n. 周边地区；附近
v. 包围；环绕；“environ”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The city's environs are filled with charming villages.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的郊区充满了迷人的村庄。
words.en: The area surrounding a place; the outskirts.

words.ex: The hapless boy lost his wallet and got caught in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 这个倒霉的男孩丢了钱包，还被雨淋了。
words.en: If you describe someone as hapless, you mean that they are unlucky or unfortunate.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；十恶不赦的
words.ex: He committed a heinous crime last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚犯下了一桩可怕的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something such as a crime as heinous, you mean that it is extremely evil or wicked.

words.tr:
adj. 隐姓埋名的；化名的
adv. 隐姓埋名地；匿名地
words.ex: He traveled incognito to avoid being recognized.
words.ex_cn: 他隐瞒身份旅行以避免被认出。
words.en: If someone does something incognito, they do it without letting people know who they are.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.ex: The king was buried in a large mausoleum.
words.ex_cn: 国王被安葬在一座巨大的陵墓中。
words.en: A mausoleum is a large and impressive building that is used as a tomb, especially for a famous person.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺；抢劫；掠夺物
v. 抢劫；掠夺
words.ex: The soldiers committed pillage after winning the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在赢得战斗后进行了掠夺。
words.en: If a group of people pillage a place, they steal a lot of things from it and often cause a lot of damage, especially in a war.

words.ex: He sat by the window in reverie.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，沉浸在遐想中。
words.en: A reverie is a state of imagining or thinking about pleasant things, often as a way of escaping from reality.

words.ex: He was held in thrall by his addiction.
words.ex_cn: 他被他的瘾所束缚。
words.en: If you say that someone is in thrall to a person or thing, you mean that they are completely in their power or are greatly influenced by them.

words.ex: The abstruse math problem confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个深奥的数学问题让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Difficult to understand; obscure.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: He acquiesced to his boss's decision.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了老板的决定。
words.en: If you acquiesce in something, you agree to do what someone wants or to accept what they do even though you may not agree with it.

words.ex: His reputation was besmirched by the false accusations.
words.ex_cn: 他的名声被这些虚假的指控玷污了。
words.en: To besmirch someone or something means to spoil their good reputation.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: His histrionic gestures made the play very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他戏剧性的手势让这场戏非常精彩。
words.en: If you refer to someone's behaviour as histrionic, you are critical of it because it is very dramatic, exaggerated, and insincere.

words.tr: n. 不适当；不正确；不得体
words.ex: His impropriety at the meeting shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的不恰当行为让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: Impropriety is the quality or state of being improper, especially in behavior or speech.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.tr:
adj. 忏悔的；悔过的
n. 忏悔者；悔罪者
words.ex: He sat in the church, a penitent man seeking forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里，一个忏悔的人寻求宽恕。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.tr: n. 弹回；反响；后果；反射
words.ex: The ball showed a clear repercussion off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上明显地弹回。
words.en: The effect that an action, event, or decision has on something, especially a bad effect.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: adj. 味道不佳的；令人讨厌的；声名狼藉的；不道德的
words.ex: The fish had an unsavory smell.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unsavory, you mean that they are unpleasant or morally unacceptable.

words.tr: n. 诅咒；受诅咒的事；逐出教门；十分讨厌的人（或事物）
words.ex: Lying is anathema to her.
words.ex_cn: 说谎是她所诅咒的。
words.en: Something or someone that one vehemently dislikes.

words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.tr: adj. 像伯伯（或叔叔）似的；长辈风范的；慈爱的
words.ex: His avuncular demeanor put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他慈祥的态度让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If someone is avuncular, they are kind and helpful towards younger or less experienced people, in a way that is typical of an uncle.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.ex: He wrote a short epigram about love.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于爱情的短小警句。
words.en: A short poem or sentence that expresses something such as a feeling or idea in a short and clever or funny way.

words.ex: He expounded his ideas clearly in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上清楚地阐述了他的观点。
words.en: To expound means to explain something in detail, especially a theory, idea, or point of view.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.tr: n. 显要人物；有权势的人；
words.ex: He is a media mogul who owns several TV channels.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位拥有多个电视频道的显要人物。
words.en: A mogul is a person who possesses a great deal of power, influence, or wealth, especially in a particular industry.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.tr: adj. 颖悟的；敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perspicacious and notices small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 她很敏锐，能注意到细小的错误。
words.en: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things.

words.tr:
n. 市侩之徒；庸俗之辈
adj. 庸俗的；没有文化教养的
words.ex: He was accused of being a philistine for his lack of interest in the arts.
words.ex_cn: 他因对艺术缺乏兴趣而被指责为没有文化教养的人。
words.en: A philistine is a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts, or who has no understanding of them.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.ex: The Philippines is an archipelago of thousands of islands.
words.ex_cn: 菲律宾是一个由数千个岛屿组成的群岛。
words.en: An archipelago is a group of islands, especially small islands, scattered in a body of water.

words.ex: The car careened off the road and into the ditch.
words.ex_cn: 汽车失控冲出道路，掉进了沟里。
words.en: To tilt or cause to tilt to one side; to lean or cause to lean to one side, especially a ship for cleaning or repair.

words.tr:
n. 骑士；勋章获得者；骑士风度的男子
adj. 傲慢的；豪强的；（对女人）献殷勤的；大方的
words.ex: The knight rode on a horse like a cavalier.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士骑着马，像个骑士一样。
words.en: If you describe someone as cavalier, you are criticizing them because you think that they do not consider other people's feelings or take account of the seriousness of a situation.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.ex: The data points correlate with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据点相互关联。
words.en: If one thing correlates with another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one thing causes the other.

words.ex: He learned the etymology of the word 'phone'.
words.ex_cn: 他学习了单词 'phone' 的词源。
words.en: Etymology is the study of the origin of words and the way in which their meanings have changed throughout history.

words.ex: The children were running in a frenetic way around the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房间里发狂似的跑来跑去。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenetic, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often not very well organized.

words.ex: The kinetic energy of the moving ball is high.
words.ex_cn: 运动的球的动能很高。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from motion.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.tr: v. 粉碎；磨成粉；彻底击败；摧毁
words.ex: The machine will pulverize the rocks into dust.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会把岩石碾成粉末。
words.en: To pulverize something means to crush it into a fine powder or to defeat someone or something completely.

words.ex: The recondite math problem confused most students.
words.ex_cn: 这道深奥的数学题让大多数学生感到困惑。
words.en: Recondite knowledge or information is known and understood by very few people.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.ex: The seismic wave shook the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震波震动了地面。
words.en: Seismic means relating to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration.

words.tr:
v. 使波动；使起伏
adj. 波动的；起伏的
words.ex: The hills undulate gently in the distance.
words.ex_cn: 远处的山丘轻轻起伏。
words.en: To move or cause to move in a smooth, wavelike motion.

words.ex: The storm caused an upheaval in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A very large change in something that often causes confusion or problems.

words.tr: v. 同意结婚；与……订婚（betroth 的过去式及过去分词）; adj. 已订婚的; n. 未婚...
words.ex: She is betrothed to a wealthy businessman.
words.ex_cn: 她与一位富有的商人订婚了。
words.en: If two people are betrothed, they have formally promised to marry each other.

words.tr: n. 亵渎上帝；亵渎神明
words.ex: He said it was blasphemy to speak against the holy book.
words.ex_cn: 他说诋毁圣书就是亵渎。
words.en: Blasphemy is the act of insulting or showing contempt or lack of reverence for a god or sacred things.

words.tr: n. 韵律；节奏；抑扬顿挫
words.ex: The dancer moved with a steady cadence.
words.ex_cn: 舞者以稳定的节奏舞动。
words.en: The rhythm or sequence of sounds or movements in speech, music, dance, etc.

words.tr: n. 教规；准则；真作集；精品集；大教堂教士
words.ex: The church follows the canon of its faith.
words.ex_cn: 教会遵循其信仰的教规。
words.en: A canon is a rule or principle that is considered to be established, accepted, or authoritative, especially in the fields of religion, literature, or law.

words.ex: The denouement of the story was surprising.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局令人惊讶。
words.en: The final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved.

words.ex: The king issued an edict to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An edict is an official order or proclamation issued by a person in authority.

words.ex: She was enamored with the beauty of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 她被日落的美景迷住了。
words.en: To fill someone with love or delight; to captivate.

words.tr: adj. 无知觉的；无感情的；无情的；愚钝的
words.ex: The insensate machine continued to operate without any human intervention.
words.ex_cn: 这台无生命的机器在没有人工干预的情况下继续运转。
words.en: If you describe someone as insensate, you mean that they lack human feelings and qualities, especially the ability to feel emotions.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.ex: He spoke a soliloquy alone on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他独自在舞台上说了一段独白。
words.en: A soliloquy is a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, often when they are alone on stage.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.tr: n. 三人领导小组；三人统治集团；三方执政集团
words.ex: The company was run by a triumvirate of experienced executives.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司由一个经验丰富的三人领导小组管理。
words.en: A triumvirate is a group of three people who share power or responsibility, especially in government.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.tr: n. 信徒；信仰者；崇拜者
words.ex: She was a devoted votary of classical music.
words.ex_cn: 她是古典音乐的虔诚崇拜者。
words.en: A votary is someone who is devoted to a particular religion, activity, or cause.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.tr: adj. 对（享乐）感到厌倦的；（因司空见惯而）无动于衷的
words.ex: He is blase about the new phone because he has one every year.
words.ex_cn: 他对新手机无动于衷，因为他每年都换一部。
words.en: If you describe someone as blasé, you mean that they are not easily impressed, excited, or worried by things, usually because they have seen or experienced them before.

words.ex: He talked with bravado, but he was scared.
words.ex_cn: 他装出勇敢的样子说话，但他其实很害怕。
words.en: A bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.ex: His domicile is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所位于纽约。
words.en: A domicile is the place where a person lives or has their home.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.tr:
n. 小人国的人；小东西
adj. 小的；矮小的
words.ex: The furniture in the dollhouse was all lilliputian, perfect for the tiny inhabitants.
words.ex_cn: 娃娃屋里的家具都是小人国的，非常适合那些小居民。
words.en: Very small; relating to Lilliput or its inhabitants; trivial or petty.

words.ex: He has a phobia of spiders.
words.ex_cn: 他有对蜘蛛的恐怖病。
words.en: A phobia is an extreme or irrational fear of or aversion to something.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.tr:
n. 抛射物；射弹；发射物；自动推进武器
adj. 发射的；射弹的；推进的
words.ex: The boy threw a projectile into the air.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把一个抛射物扔向空中。
words.en: A projectile is an object that is thrown or shot forwards, such as a bullet fired from a gun.

words.tr: adj. 恶心的；欲吐的；稍感紧张的；略有不安的
words.ex: He feels queasy after eating too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖果后感到恶心。
words.en: If you feel queasy, you feel slightly sick or uncomfortable, especially because you are nervous or worried.

words.tr: v. 回报；报答；往复；来回
words.ex: She helped me, and I will reciprocate.
words.ex_cn: 她帮了我，我会回报她。
words.en: If your feelings or actions towards someone are reciprocated, the other person feels or behaves in the same way towards you as you have felt or behaved towards them.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.ex: He felt vertigo after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕。
words.en: A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, associated particularly with looking down from a great height, or caused by disease affecting the inner ear or the vestibular nerve; giddiness.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The attrition between the two rocks caused sparks.
words.ex_cn: 两块岩石之间的摩擦产生了火花。
words.en: Attrition refers to the process of reducing something's strength or effectiveness through sustained attack or pressure, or the gradual reduction in the number of employees in an organization by retirement, resignation, or death.

words.ex: The team's loss was a total debacle.
words.ex_cn: 球队的失败是一场彻底的惨败。
words.en: A debacle is a sudden and complete failure or collapse, often in a way that is very embarrassing or causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: The chemicals were used to defoliate the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质被用来使树木落叶。
words.en: To remove the leaves from a plant or tree, especially by using chemicals.

words.ex: He is an equestrian rider who trains every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天早上训练的骑马者。
words.en: An equestrian is someone who rides horses, especially as a sport or a profession.

words.ex: The court decided to expunge his record.
words.ex_cn: 法院决定删除他的记录。
words.en: If you expunge something, you get rid of it completely, because it causes problems or bad feelings.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老生常谈的
words.ex: His jokes are hackneyed and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话陈腐又无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as hackneyed, you mean that it is unoriginal and has been used so often that it is no longer interesting.

words.ex: He faced opprobrium for lying to the public.
words.ex_cn: 他因对公众撒谎而遭到谴责。
words.en: Opprobrium is harsh criticism or censure; public disgrace arising from shameful conduct.

words.ex: The contract has a proviso that payments must be made on time.
words.ex_cn: 合同中有一项限制条款，要求付款必须按时进行。
words.en: A proviso is a condition or stipulation in a legal document, agreement, or law that must be fulfilled or adhered to.

words.ex: He sullied his reputation by lying.
words.ex_cn: 他通过撒谎玷污了自己的声誉。
words.en: To sully something means to spoil or reduce the value of something, especially someone's reputation or the purity of something.

words.tr: adj. 触觉的；能触知的；手感好的
words.ex: The child learns through tactile objects like blocks.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过触觉物体如积木来学习。
words.en: Relating to the sense of touch; perceptible by touch.

words.ex: She upbraided him for his carelessness.
words.ex_cn: 她因他的粗心大意而责骂他。
words.en: To criticize or reproach severely; to scold.

words.ex: The verdant hills looked beautiful in spring.
words.ex_cn: 青翠的山丘在春天看起来很美。
words.en: Green with grass or other rich vegetation.

words.ex: The vertex of the triangle is at the top.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的顶点在顶部。
words.en: The highest point of something; the top or apex.

words.tr: v. 使减细；使减小；使减弱
words.ex: The wire attenuates as it gets longer.
words.ex_cn: 这根电线随着变长而变细。
words.en: To reduce the force, effect, or value of something.

words.tr: n. 巨兽；庞然大物；巨头
words.ex: The company is a behemoth in the tech industry.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是科技行业中的巨无霸。
words.en: A behemoth is something that is extremely large and powerful, often referring to an organization, project, or thing that is so large it is difficult to manage or control.

words.ex: They disinterred the body last week.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周把尸体挖了出来。
words.en: To dig up something that has been buried, especially a corpse.

words.ex: The new law impinges on people's privacy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律侵犯了人们的隐私。
words.en: To impinge means to have an effect or influence, especially a negative one, on someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.ex: He called the test a 'silent scream', which is an oxymoron.
words.ex_cn: 他把这次考试称为‘无声的尖叫’，这是一个矛盾修辞法。
words.en: An oxymoron is a figure of speech in which apparently contradictory terms appear in conjunction.

words.ex: The garden was in a state of plenitude, with flowers blooming everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，处处充满生机。
words.en: The state of being full or complete; abundance.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.ex: The meat will putrefy if left in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 如果把肉放在阳光下，它会腐烂。
words.en: To decay or cause to decay and have a foul smell.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.ex: Reindeer live in the tundra near the North Pole.
words.ex_cn: 驯鹿生活在北极附近的苔原上。
words.en: A tundra is a vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.tr: n. (人生的)盛衰；（人生的）盛衰（vicissitude 的复数）；
words.ex: He faced many vicissitudes in life, from wealth to poverty.
words.ex_cn: 他一生经历了许多盛衰，从富有到贫穷。
words.en: The changes and difficulties that happen in a situation or in a person's life.

words.ex: The treaty established amity between the two nations.
words.ex_cn: 该条约确立了两国之间的友好关系。
words.en: A friendly relationship between people or countries.

words.ex: He made an animadversion on his friend's poor choice.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的糟糕选择提出了批评。
words.en: A critical or censorious remark or comment.

words.ex: His views are antithetical to hers.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与她的观点是对偶的。
words.en: Directly opposed or contrasted; mutually incompatible.

words.ex: He is bellicose when he drinks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了时就好战。
words.en: Having or showing a tendency to argue or fight.

words.ex: He loves the bucolic life in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢乡村的田园生活。
words.en: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.ex: Writing became her métier after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 经过多年的练习，写作成了她的专长。
words.en: A métier is a profession or occupation, especially one that you are good at and enjoy.

words.ex: He is penurious and never tips the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他很吝啬，从不给服务员小费。
words.en: If you describe someone as penurious, you mean that they are extremely poor or extremely unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: The family endured years of privation during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭在战争期间经历了多年的贫困。
words.en: Privation is a situation in which you do not have the things that are essential for a comfortable life, such as enough food, clothing, or shelter.

words.ex: He was known by his sobriquet 'The Great Communicator'.
words.ex_cn: 他被称为绰号“伟大的沟通者”。
words.en: A sobriquet is a nickname or a familiar name, often a descriptive one, that is given to a person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.ex: He was in the throes of a difficult decision.
words.ex_cn: 他正处在艰难抉择的痛苦中。
words.en: If someone is experiencing something very unpleasant or emotionally painful, you can say that they are in the throes of it.

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.ex: Two events happen concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.ex: His crass joke made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他愚蠢的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as crass, you mean they are so stupid and insensitive that they offend you.

words.ex: Italian cuisine is famous for pasta and pizza.
words.ex_cn: 意大利烹调风格以意大利面和披萨闻名。
words.en: A style or method of cooking, especially as characteristic of a particular country, region, or establishment.

words.ex: He tried to debase the coin with cheap metal.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用廉价金属贬低硬币的价值。
words.en: To debase something means to reduce its value or quality.

words.ex: The judge enjoin him from selling the house.
words.ex_cn: 法官禁止他出售这所房子。
words.en: If a judge enjoins someone from doing something, they order them not to do it. If a judge enjoins an action, they order people not to do it.

words.tr: adj. 即席的；临时的；无准备的；不用讲稿的
words.ex: He gave an extemporaneous speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: spoken or done without preparation

words.ex: The genesis of the story is a simple dream.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的起源是一个简单的梦。
words.en: The origin or mode of formation of something.

words.tr: n. 饮酒；奠酒祭神仪式（形容词 libationary）
words.ex: They poured a libation to honor the gods.
words.ex_cn: 他们倒酒祭神，以示敬意。
words.en: A libation is a ritual pouring of a liquid as an offering to a god or spirit, or in memory of those who have died.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: The storm sundered the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树劈开了。
words.en: To break or split apart, especially along a natural line or grain.

words.tr:
n. 艰辛；艰苦劳动；痛苦；分娩的阵痛
v. 辛苦工作；发生或经受阵痛
words.ex: His travail helped him succeed in the end.
words.ex_cn: 他的艰辛最终让他取得了成功。
words.en: Travail refers to painful or laborious effort, especially in the context of work or childbirth.

words.ex: The project is in abeyance until next year.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目暂时搁置，直到明年。
words.en: A state of temporary disuse or suspension.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.tr: adj. 拖拉的；拖沓的；磨蹭的
words.ex: He gave a dilatory answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题回答得很拖拉。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dilatory, you mean that they are slow and cause delay.

words.tr: adj. 基督教大联合的；普世的；普遍的
words.ex: The ecumenical movement seeks to promote unity among all Christian churches.
words.ex_cn: 普世运动旨在促进所有基督教会之间的团结。
words.en: Ecumenical is used to describe something that is concerned with promoting unity among the world's different Christian churches.

words.ex: The old building has a beautiful facade with stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老建筑有一个带有石柱的漂亮正面。
words.en: The front of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. Also, a superficial appearance or illusion of something.

words.ex: The gargoyles on the church tower looked menacing.
words.ex_cn: 教堂塔楼上的滴水嘴看起来很凶恶。
words.en: A grotesque carved human or animal face or figure projecting from the gutter of a building, typically acting as a spout to carry water clear of a wall.

words.tr:
adj. 未决议的；有讨论余地的
v. 提出…供讨论
words.ex: The issue is still a moot point.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题仍然是未决的。
words.en: If a plan, idea, or subject is mooted, it is suggested or introduced for discussion.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.ex: The choir performed a beautiful requiem in memory of the deceased.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班为纪念逝者演唱了一首优美的安魂曲。
words.en: A requiem is a piece of music that is performed in a Catholic church in memory of someone who has died, or a piece of music that is similar to this and is performed in memory of someone who has died.

words.tr: adj. 极神圣的；神圣不可侵犯的
words.ex: The church's rules were considered sacrosanct and unchangeable.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的规定被认为是神圣不可侵犯的，不可改变的。
words.en: If you describe something as sacrosanct, you mean that it is considered to be special and should not be changed or interfered with.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.tr: n. 仲裁人；公断人；权威
words.ex: He is the arbiter of the dispute.
words.ex_cn: 他是这场纠纷的仲裁者。
words.en: An arbiter is a person or agency officially appointed to settle a dispute.

words.ex: The cardinals met in conclave to elect a new pope.
words.ex_cn: 红衣主教们秘密开会选举新教皇。
words.en: A conclave is a private meeting at which the discussions are kept secret, especially a meeting of Roman Catholic cardinals to elect a new pope.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.tr: n. 小团体；小圈子；志同道合的一伙
words.ex: He belongs to a small coterie of artists.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个小艺术家圈子的成员。
words.en: A coterie is a small group of people with shared interests or tastes, especially one that is exclusive of other people.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: He likes to flaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: If you flaunt something, you show it off in a way that is intended to attract people's attention and make them envious.

words.tr: adj. 文雅的；有教养的；上流社会的；装绅士派头的
words.ex: She spoke in a genteel way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上说话很文雅。
words.en: Someone who is genteel behaves in a polite and refined way, often in a manner that is considered typical of someone from a high social class.

words.ex: The story had a graphic description of the battle.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事对战斗的描述非常生动。
words.en: A graphic is a visual representation of data or information, such as a chart, diagram, or picture.

words.ex: The company's policies were inimical to the interests of its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司的政策对员工的利益是有害的。
words.en: If one thing is inimical to another, it prevents the second thing from happening or being successful, or it is harmful to it.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.tr: n. 寡头政治；寡头统治集团；寡头统治的国家
words.ex: The country is ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy businessmen.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群富有的商人寡头统治。
words.en: A form of government in which all power is vested in a few persons or in a dominant class or clique; government by the few.

words.ex: The redoubtable warrior struck fear into the hearts of his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 那位令人敬畏的战士让敌人心生恐惧。
words.en: If you describe someone as redoubtable, you have great respect for their power and strength, and you may be afraid of them as well.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；讨厌的；抵触的
words.ex: The smell was repugnant.
words.ex_cn: 那气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you think that something is horrible and disgusting, you can say that it is repugnant.

words.ex: The old letters are kept in the city archives.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧信件保存在城市的档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.ex: The estate included both real estate and chattels.
words.ex_cn: 该地产包括了房地产和动产。
words.en: A chattel is a personal possession, as opposed to real estate, or a slave.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: The conflagration destroyed the whole forest.
words.ex_cn: 这场大火烧毁了整个森林。
words.en: A conflagration is a large and destructive fire that causes considerable damage.

words.tr: n. 林波舞；不稳定状态；中间过渡状态
words.ex: The project is currently in limbo while we wait for approval.
words.ex_cn: 该项目目前处于待批准的中间状态。
words.en: A situation of uncertainty or neglect, especially one regarded as being in a state of waiting or not progressing.

words.ex: He traced his lineage back to ancient kings.
words.ex_cn: 他追溯了自己的家系到古代的国王。
words.en: Your lineage is the series of families from which you are directly descended.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 摇摇欲坠的；破烂不堪的
words.ex: The old house was ramshackle and needed repair.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子摇摇欲坠，需要修理。
words.en: A ramshackle building or vehicle is in very bad condition and in danger of falling down.

words.ex: The jury was sequestered during the trial.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团在审判期间被隔离。
words.en: To sequester means to isolate or hide away; it can also refer to the legal process of seizing property until a debt is paid or a dispute is resolved.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.ex: The virulent virus spread quickly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种剧毒的病毒迅速在小镇上传播。
words.en: A virulent disease or poison is extremely powerful and dangerous.

words.ex: The autocratic leader made all decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁的领导人独自做出所有决定，从不询问他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as autocratic, you are criticizing them because they have complete power and make decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.tr: adj. 搞两面派的；奸诈的；骗人的
words.ex: He gave a duplicitous answer to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个虚伪的回答来隐藏真相。
words.en: Someone who is duplicitous is deceitful.

words.ex: The king sent an emissary to talk to the neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 国王派了一名使者去与邻国交谈。
words.en: An emissary is a person who is sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representative.

words.tr: adj. 贴切的；恰当的；妥帖的
words.ex: His felicitous remark made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 他得体的言论让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Well chosen or suited to the circumstances.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

words.tr: adj. 没有钱的；身无分文的；贫穷的
words.ex: The impecunious student had to rely on scholarships to continue his education.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的学生不得不依靠奖学金来继续他的学业。
words.en: If you describe someone as impecunious, you mean that they have very little money.

words.tr:
adj. 患黄疸病的；有偏见的
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见；“jaundice”的过去式
words.ex: His judgment was jaundiced by his personal dislike for the candidate.
words.ex_cn: 他对候选人的个人反感使他的判断带有偏见。
words.en: If someone has a jaundiced view of something, they see it in a negative way because they are jealous or bitter.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.tr: adj. 小气的；吝啬的；太节省的
words.ex: His parsimonious nature made him unpopular among colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他吝啬的本性使得他在同事中不受欢迎。
words.en: Someone who is parsimonious is very unwilling to spend money.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.tr:
adj. 被剥夺的；丧失的；失去亲人的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was bereft of words after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他一句话也说不出来。
words.en: If someone is bereft of something, they have lost it and feel its loss keenly.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.ex: He had the effrontery to lie to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老师撒谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as effrontery, you are emphasizing that it is very rude or disrespectful.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.ex: He criticized others for lying, but his own actions showed hypocrisy.
words.ex_cn: 他批评别人撒谎，但自己的行为却表现出虚伪。
words.en: The practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behavior does not conform; pretense.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；迫在眉睫的； v. “impend”的现在分词；
words.ex: An impending storm made people stay indoors.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴让人们待在室内。
words.en: If an event or situation is impending, it is about to happen or is likely to happen very soon.

words.tr:
adj. 愤怒的；激怒了的
v. 使愤怒；激怒；“incense”的过去式与过去分词
words.ex: He was incensed when they lied to him.
words.ex_cn: 当他们对他撒谎时，他非常愤怒。
words.en: If you are incensed by something, it makes you extremely angry.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.ex: He feared retribution for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕因自己的行为而受到报复。
words.en: Retribution is punishment for a crime, especially punishment that is carried out by someone other than the official authorities.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.ex: The company operates under the aegis of the government.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是在政府的保护下运营的。
words.en: The protection, backing, or support of a particular person or organization.

words.tr: n. 低廉花哨的首饰；美观而无价值的东西
words.ex: She wore a necklace adorned with colorful baubles.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条饰有彩色小饰物的项链。
words.en: A bauble is a small, cheap ornament or piece of jewelry.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: The depredation of forests harms wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 森林的破坏危害了野生动物。
words.en: The act of preying upon or plundering; the act of laying waste; as, the depredations of an army on the country.

words.ex: The saint had an epiphany while praying in the church.
words.ex_cn: 圣人在教堂祈祷时经历了显灵。
words.en: An epiphany is a moment of sudden and great revelation or realization.

words.ex: The government declared a moratorium on new construction.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布暂停新的建筑项目。
words.en: A moratorium is a temporary prohibition of an activity.

words.tr: adj. 松垂的；悬垂摆动的
words.ex: The pendulous branches swayed in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 垂下的枝条在风中摇曳。
words.en: Something that is pendulous hangs or swings freely.

words.ex: Dark clouds portend a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something portends something else, it indicates that it is likely to happen in the future.

words.tr: adj. 务实的；实事求是的；
words.ex: He took a pragmatic approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了务实的方法来解决问题。
words.en: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

words.tr:
v. 缓期执行；暂缓处刑
n. 缓刑；暂缓
words.ex: The judge gave him a reprieve until next month.
words.ex_cn: 法官给了他一个延期，直到下个月。
words.en: If someone who has been sentenced in a court is given a reprieve, their punishment is officially delayed or cancelled.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；声音极大的
words.ex: His stentorian voice filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 他洪亮的声音充满了整个房间。
words.en: A stentorian voice is very loud and powerful.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: He is ambidextrous and can write with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他是左右手都灵巧的，可以用两只手写字。
words.en: Someone who is ambidextrous can use both their right and left hands equally well.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: The child excoriated his knee when he fell on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒在粗糙的地面上，膝盖擦伤了。
words.en: To excoriate someone or something means to criticize them severely.

words.ex: He extrapolates the trend from last year's data.
words.ex_cn: 他从去年的数据中推断出趋势。
words.en: To extrapolate is to estimate or conclude something by extending or projecting known information.

words.ex: The crime scene was grisly and made everyone feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 犯罪现场很可怕，让所有人都感到恶心。
words.en: Grisly is used to describe something that is extremely unpleasant and horrifying, often because it involves death or violence.

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.ex: They impute the failure to poor planning.
words.ex_cn: 他们把失败归因于计划不周。
words.en: If you impute something such as blame or a crime to someone, you say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.

words.tr:
adj. 笨拙的；不机敏的；笨手笨脚的
n. 一个笨拙愚蠢的人
words.ex: He was maladroit when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: If you describe someone as maladroit, you mean that they are clumsy or awkward, especially in social situations.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；已过盛年的
words.ex: The fashion styles of the 1980s are now considered passé.
words.ex_cn: 20世纪80年代的时尚风格现在被认为已经过时了。
words.en: No longer fashionable or in vogue; out of date.

words.tr: n. 施教者；好为人师的人；卖弄学问者
words.ex: The pedagogue taught children to read and write.
words.ex_cn: 这位教师教孩子们读书写字。
words.en: A pedagogue is a teacher, especially one who is strict or old-fashioned in their methods.

words.ex: The preponderance of evidence shows he is guilty.
words.ex_cn: 大多数证据表明他有罪。
words.en: If there is a preponderance of one type of thing or person in a group, there are more of that type than of any other.

words.tr: v. 提出；提议；提出…供考虑
words.ex: He propound a new theory in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上提出了一种新理论。
words.en: To propound means to suggest or put forward an idea, theory, or point of view for consideration.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.
